recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. The current source satisfies the final Jira decision, and adding more prose would mostly duplicate existing guidance and increase maintenance drift.
issue_request: FHIR-27085 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution asking for guidance on how one server can support multiple profiles, including profiles that prohibit elements, use different bindings, or include jurisdiction-specific extensions. The resolution cited CapabilityStatement.rest.resource.supportedProfile for declaring multiple profiles and asked for profiling best practices that discourage prohibiting optional elements and discourage excluding additional Codings.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-27085 was found. The relevant guidance appears to have been applied implicitly by commit 6616e51d37fe83bbfebcdb574deb3ccc2cae86a3, which added the broader-compatibility paragraph to source/profiling.html but used a misleading FHIR-27115 subject. Current CapabilityStatement source also already documents supportedProfile as the repeatable use-case-specific profile declaration mechanism.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread records the original implementer concern: globally deployed servers are made harder by profiles that remove fields or disallow extra codings, and explicit best-practice guidance would help. FHIR-I minutes for 2020-08-17 record the FHIR-27085 Persuasive with Modification vote. FHIR-27115 is unrelated event-basedOn extension work and already has its own combined-branch audit, so it was not decided again.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/profiling.html already contains the Supporting Multiple Profiles section, including the non-overlapping profile model and guidance to avoid prohibiting unnecessary elements, allow additional Codings, and prefer extensible/preferred bindings when possible. source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml already describes supportedProfile as a list of use-case-specific profiles that may differ by resource handling.

related_jiras.note: A historical commit adding the FHIR-27085 guidance was mislabeled FHIR-27115, but the actual FHIR-27115 issue concerns event-basedOn extension context and is already represented separately on the combined branch.
